Package org.apache.juneau.commons.beanquery

Interface Filter

All Known Implementing Classes:
Filter.And, Filter.Leaf, Filter.Not, Filter.Or
public sealed interface Filter permits Filter.Leaf, Filter.And, Filter.Or, Filter.Not
A resolved, engine-neutral search tree (design §7) — the ResolvedQuery.filter() replacement for the earlier flat Term/terms() list.

QueryResolver builds this tree from a request's raw search string: it parses the string with SearchParser into a SearchItem tree, then resolves every leaf's column (against the context's allow-list) and expression (with SearchExpressionParser, using that column's operator set), carrying the column's SearchType along for the engine to use. An empty search resolves to an empty Filter.And (design §7) — not null — so every engine can treat "no search" as just another tree to evaluate, one that matches every row.

Both engines walk this same shape: InMemoryBeanQuerySession evaluates it recursively against one row; SqlSearchCompiler (not linkable from here — it lives in the separate juneau-beanquery-sql module, which this one does not depend on) renders it to a parenthesized SQL boolean expression. Neither engine ever sees a raw request string or an unresolved column name.

Example:

// ageExpr/nameExpr/emailExpr are already-resolved SearchExpressions, e.g. from SearchExpressionParser.parse() // (age > 21) AND (name CONTAINS "bob" OR email CONTAINS "bob") Filter f = new Filter.And(List.of( new Filter.Leaf("age", ageExpr, SearchType.NUMERIC), new Filter.Or(List.of( new Filter.Leaf("name", nameExpr, SearchType.TEXT), new Filter.Leaf("email", emailExpr, SearchType.TEXT)))));

Unlike the package-private SearchItem it mirrors, Filter is public: SqlSearchCompiler (above) lives in juneau-beanquery-sql, a separate module downstream of this one, and must be able to pattern-match over this tree directly.
